title: Framing embroidery
subtitle: How to mount and stretch a finished embroidery ready for a frame.
excerpt: Mounting embroidery involves stretching the blocked piece over acid-free mounting board and securing it at the back before framing. The method is lacing: thread is worked back and forth across the back of the board to hold the fabric in constant tension. This produces a flat, stable mount that won't sag.
sourceNotes: Framing and mounting technique synthesised from contemporary needlework finishing practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: The method of securing fabric to a mounting board by weaving strong thread back and forth across the back of the board, through the fabric edges, to hold the piece under even tension. Lacing is more stable than stapling and causes less distortion.

content.text: an embroidery onto acid-free mounting board keeps the piece stable for years without the risk of rust from staples or warping from tape. The process takes about 20 minutes but the result is significantly more durable than stapled mounts.
Acid-free mounting board, cut to the size of the framed area. Strong thread: linen or polyester carpet thread works well. A long tapestry needle. The blocked and dried embroidery.
Centre the embroidery over the mounting board, face down. Fold the surplus fabric over the board edges.

Starting at the centre of the top and bottom edges, thread strong thread and lace across the back of the board, picking up the turned-over fabric edges alternately top and bottom. Work toward one corner, then return from the centre to the other corner.
Pull the lacing firmly but evenly. The fabric should be taut across the front of the board.
Repeat the lacing process across the other axis (left-right), working from the centre outward on each side.
Secure all thread ends with a few backstitches. Turn the board face up and check the embroidery is centred and the grain is straight before placing in the frame.

items.symptom: The embroidery is off-centre in the frame
items.cause: The design was not centred on the mounting board before lacing began.
items.fix: Mark the centre of the board and the centre of the embroidery before starting. Align the two before folding over the edges.

items.symptom: The fabric sags away from the board
items.cause: The lacing thread was not pulled tight enough or the thread stretched after tying off.
items.fix: Use a non-stretch thread such as linen or polyester for lacing. Retighten and re-tie if the lacing has loosened.
